sections.h2: How is Terrell County laid out, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Terrell sits in southwest Georgia on 338 square miles, with Dawson as its seat and its only city. Wikipedia dates the county to February 16, 1856 and says it was named for William Terrell. The three towns are Bronwood, Parrott and Sasser.

Ichawaynochaway Creek drains the western and southern two thirds, and the Kinchafoonee-Muckalee system takes the northeast. U.S. 82 is the main route, joined by State Routes 32, 41, 45, 49, 50, 55, 118 and 520. Webster, Sumter, Lee, Dougherty, Calhoun and Randolph counties form the borders.

The county is shrinking. The Census Bureau tallied 9,185 residents in 2020 and puts the July 2025 estimate at 8,656, down 5.7% from its base. That leaves roughly 27 people per square mile, so a listing may be a farmhouse with acreage or a small house on a Dawson lot.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Terrell County housing?
sections.html:
Owners hold a middle value of $118,400 on their homes for 2020-2024, and they occupy 61.6% of occupied housing. Renters face a middle gross rent of $745.

Five permits and a same-house share of 92.8% describe a settled, aging stock. One resident in four is past 65, so estates are a regular source of listings. The profile also counts 3,383 households of about 2.53 people and a 22.6 minute average trip to work.

sections.h2: Which Terrell County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner works from 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson and takes mail at P.O. Box 484, Dawson, GA 39842. The tax website shows (229) 995-5151 and counter hours of 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays.

  • Tax commissioner, (229) 995-5151: bills, payments, penalties and levies.
  • Tax assessor, (229) 995-5210, P.O. Box 382: values, returns, homestead filings, mobile home registration.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, courthouse deed room: copies of a warranty deed.
  • Commissioners' office, (229) 995-4476: curbside trash for homes outside the four municipalities.

First-time homeowners are told to bring a copy of the warranty deed when they apply for homestead, so a new buyer should pick one up from the deed room before going to the assessors.

sections.h2: What is Terrell County's due date, November 15 or December 20?
sections.html:
The county's own pages differ, so trust the notice in your mailbox. The general information page says December 20, and the FAQ says real estate and business personal property taxes have been due November 15 since 2018. Both put mobile homes at April 1.

The general information page describes the late steps for real estate in this order:

  • Interest is added on the 2nd of every month, at prime plus 3% divided by 12.
  • A FIFA lien goes on file with the Clerk of Courts 30 days after the date on the delinquent notice.
  • A 5% penalty arrives after 120 days and repeats every 120 days to a 20% ceiling.
  • An account still open goes to a collection firm, which adds administrative and levy fees of up to $240.00 plus.

Those fees pay for certified notices and a title search that prepares the parcel for sale. The property is advertised four weeks in the Herald Journal before the auction. A mailed payment counts if the United States Postal Service postmarked it, while a metered mark does not.

sections.h2: How are Terrell County mobile homes taxed?
sections.html:
A mobile or modular home counts as personal property. If it sits in the county on January 1, tax is due April 1 and the owner gets a location permit then. Bills usually go out on January 2.

Missing April 1 costs a 10% penalty, and the county may cite the owner into Magistrate Court or sell the home. An overdue account gains interest on the 16th of each month, takes the 10% penalty on April 2, and gets a FIFA 30 days after the delinquent notice. The decal has to be displayed, and the assessors answer questions at (229) 995-5210.

If the home changes hands during the tax year, ask which owner paid the permit tax before the closing date.

sections.h2: What exemptions and appeal routes exist in Terrell County?
sections.html:
Homestead filings go to the Board of Tax Assessors, and you must own and live in the home as of January 1. The form can be filed any time of year, but it needs to arrive by April 1 to count for that year. After approval it runs until you move.

The tax website says Terrell County has local exemptions, and the local amount takes over from the state amount when it is greater. Ask the assessors for today's figures. Owners 62 and over may qualify for additional relief, and a deferral program allows owners 62 and over with gross household income of $15,000 or less to postpone tax until ownership changes or the deferred tax and interest hit 85% of fair market value.

Farm programs assess qualifying agricultural land at 30 percent rather than 40, and Conservation Use values land by how it is used. Each needs a covenant of at least ten years.

Appeals start within 45 days of the notice date, on grounds of taxability, value or uniformity. Disagreements go to the Board of Equalization or arbitration, then Superior Court. A friend or relative may file within 90 days for an owner serving in the armed forces.

sections.h2: Do Terrell County business owners file returns too?
sections.html:
Yes. Personal property returns on form PT-50p go to the Board of Assessors every year, whatever the change in value or use. The tax site warns that an owner who no longer has a listed item must tell the assessors or keep being taxed on it, and that a missing required real estate return carries a 10% penalty on the value not returned.

Equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40 percent of fair market value. Manufacturers can claim the freeport exemption on raw goods, goods in process, or finished goods stored for out-of-state shipment, with applications filed between January 1 and April 1.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes before selling in Terrell County?
sections.html:
Phone the commissioner at (229) 995-5151 and ask for a written balance on each year, mobile home accounts included. Ask whether a FIFA has been recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, since a lien has to be paid off for the deed to record cleanly.

Georgia measures value as of January 1, and the commissioner can explain how it will bill the year you sell. Mention every open item to the title company early, because a lien found at the closing table delays the date. Accounts that reached the collection stage are costlier, since the administrative and levy fees ride on top of the balance.

A buyer paying cash for the house as it stands can pay tax out of your proceeds and close without repairs.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Terrell County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: (229) 995-5151. The office is at 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson, open 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays, with P.O. Box 484 for mail.

faqs.q: Is the Terrell County due date November 15 or December 20?
faqs.a: The county's pages disagree: the general information page says December 20, and the FAQ says November 15 starting in 2018. Follow the date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: What is the Terrell County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year you want the exemption. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and bring your deed if you are a first-time homeowner.

faqs.q: How soon must I appeal a Terrell County assessment?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the notice date. Grounds are taxability, value or uniformity, and a complaint about the amount of tax is not a ground.

faqs.q: What if I skip a Terrell County tax payment?
faqs.a: Interest starts on the 2nd of the following month, a FIFA lien follows after 30 days from the delinquent notice, and a 5% penalty builds every 120 days to 20%. A long unpaid account goes to a collection firm and can end in a sale.
